Today we’re releasing OCRia-1, a frontier VLM for document parsing that sets a new SOTA in accuracy, cost, and latency. 

It not only sets a new high score on ParseBench (87.4), but also leads in three 3rd-party benchmarks: olmOCR-bench* (83.5 overall, 92.9 on tables!), PulseBench-Tab (84.1), and fr-bench-pdf2md (72.1).

OCRia-1 is really, really good at parsing complex tables: nested headers, merged cells, irregular grids, scanned tables, and more. It is also fantastic at parsing complex unlabeled charts (line, bar, pie, technical diagrams), and preserving complex formatting. Most real-world enterprise documents contain at least one of the these, whether it’s a big tax withholding table or a public economic report.

It is a 4B model and outperforms all other models within a similar parameter class: LightOnOCR-3, Chandra-OCR 2, Mistral OCR 4.1, and more. It is also extremely fast.

All credit goes to our research team, who spent countless hours on curating a diverse dataset, tuning our training pipeline, and squeezing every last drop out of model optimization so that it can process billions of pages at scale. 

OCRia-1 as a base is powering all of our modes within LlamaParse (cost-effective, agentic, agentic plus), so you can access its capabilities today! 

If you’re processing millions/billions of documents at scale, we’re offering enterprises that book a demo up to $3k in credits for a guided evaluation.**

*olmOCR-bench scores are adjusted based on unifying rendering at 1,288px for all models 
**enterprise POC credits apply to eligible organizations that book a demo

posts.text:
While I was writing this, my AI assistant got cut off by a bio safety filter. It was summarizing my own team's notes on the model we released today 😅

Frontier labs are moving fast into biology but the scientists and clinicians who'd get the most out of these models are unfortunately the ones running into walls like this one (and every day).

So we partnered with TIGEM (Telethon Institute of Genetics and Medicine), Naple "Federico II" University and Zhongguancun Academy to train Carbon-X.

Carbon-X is an open 14B model that reads raw DNA and talks about it in plain English. On our DNA benchmarks it scores 67%, vs 61% for Claude Opus 5.5 and 50% for Gemini 4 Argon, and its within a point of GPT-6.1 Sol at about 1000x lower cost.

We kept human and animal viruses out of the training data. The weights are open and the model runs on hardware accessible to academia (a laptop).

One example from the blog: give frontier models an 8kb stretch of the NF1 gene with a mutation at a splice site. Most of them call it benign, refuse, or run out of tokens. Carbon-X says pathogenic, because the mutation breaks the splice site.

This century, biology may be where AI matters most. We want to get there with the safety work done in the open and every lab in the world able to build on it. Go try it, and tell us what you find.

写这段文字时，我的 AI 助手被生物安全过滤器中断了。当时它只是在总结我们团队关于今天发布的模型的笔记 😅

前沿实验室正在快速进军生物学，但遗憾的是，最能从这些模型中受益的科学家和临床医生，却恰恰每天都在遭遇这样的阻碍。

因此，我们与 TIGEM（Telethon 遗传与医学研究所）、那不勒斯费德里科二世大学和中关村学院合作，训练了 Carbon-X。

Carbon-X 是一款开放的 14B 模型，能读取原始 DNA 序列，并用通俗英语加以解释。在我们的 DNA 基准测试中，它获得了 67% 的分数，而 Claude Opus 5.5 为 61%，Gemini 4 Argon 为 50%；它与 GPT-6.1 Sol 的分差不到 1 个百分点，成本却仅为其约千分之一。

我们在训练数据中排除了人类和动物病毒。模型权重开放，并且可在学术界容易获得的硬件（一台笔记本电脑）上运行。

博客中有这样一个例子：向前沿模型提供一段长 8kb、剪接位点存在突变的 NF1 基因序列。大多数模型要么判断为良性，要么拒绝回答，要么耗尽 token。Carbon-X 则判断其具有致病性，因为该突变破坏了剪接位点。

在本世纪，生物学可能是 AI 最能发挥作用的领域。我们希望以公开开展安全研究、让全球每个实验室都能在此基础上继续构建的方式，实现这一目标。欢迎试用，并告诉我们你的发现。

Agent Harness 也开始学「面向对象编程」了。

Google Cloud AI Research 和 UIUC 这篇 OO-Harness，把 Harness 组织成一棵可以持续进化的类继承树。

不同任务需要的执行策略并不一样。与其不断修改一套全局 Harness，OO-Harness 会先从执行轨迹里找到相似的失败模式，再为这类任务生成一个专门的子类。

公共能力从父类继承，特殊需求只改对应方法。

到了新任务，Router 会先观察基础 Harness 的执行轨迹，再决定继续用 Base，还是切到某个专用 Harness。

这个设计还有一个挺实用的好处：

遇到完全陌生的 OOD 任务时，Router 可以直接退回原始 Base，避免之前学到的「优化」反过来拖累新任务。

实验覆盖 AutomationBench、Workspace-Bench 和 Toolathlon-GYM，OO-Harness 三项都拿到最佳结果。

其中 AutomationBench 从 61.62 提升到 77.41；消融里，真正使用继承结构也比扁平复制 Harness 高近 5 个百分点。

这样的话，Harness 开始有了「分支」和「继承」。

以后面对越来越复杂的任务，Agent 可能不会再共用一套万能工作流。

它的运行系统会像软件架构一样，逐渐长出不同分支，再根据任务选择最合适的一条。

posts.text:
一个错误如果被 Agent 总结成 Skill，下一次它可能会更自信地再犯一遍。

《More Memory, Worse Agents》研究的就是这种 Error Reproduction。

很多 Agent Memory 会把过去轨迹总结成规则和经验，再用于后续任务。问题在于，一旦总结本身出了偏差，错误也会跟着长期保存，并继续影响之后的决策。

作者因此提出 Anti-Persistence：

真实轨迹和结果可以长期保存，但抽象出来的规则和策略只在当前任务临时生成，用完就丢。下一次再根据新的上下文重新总结。

实验覆盖 ALFWorld、WebShop 和 ScienceWorld。Anti-Persistence 在 9 个模型×任务组合里拿到 7 个最好结果，平均成功率 59.9%，同时 LLM 调用成本最低。

长期保存，并不天然等于长期学习。我的判断是：该长期存的是事实（轨迹和结果），而不是结论（规则和策略）。结论随时可以重新算，存错了却很难发现。

做 Agent Memory 或 Skill 自进化的可以先收藏。我会先检查自己的 Memory 里存的是原始轨迹还是总结出的规则；如果是规则，至少给每条记上来源轨迹，出错时能追回去。

如果某类错误在接入 Memory 之后反而更频繁了，先怀疑的就该是那几条总结出来的规则。

广告 Agent 和 ChatGPT 正常回答并行运行。即便广告竞价成功，只要来晚了就直接放弃，绝不拖慢用户的回复。

Instead of third-party agents scraping logins, @PaymanAI deploys AI agents inside the bank, on the institution’s existing systems.

In practice, that means a customer can say “Pay my ConEd bill” or “Move $1,850 to cover rent” and get it done in seconds, with confirmation - under the bank’s brand, policies, and oversight. Community banks are already partnering with them (Middlesex Federal, Citizens State Bank in Colorado). It’s backed by Visa, Coinbase Ventures, and Circle, and it recently won the ICBA ThinkTECH Banker’s Choice Award.

This story shows what happens when AI meets banking without a trust layer: chaos, blocks, and lost convenience. Payman is the missing piece, the orchestration layer that lets people get the helpful AI banking experience they want, while giving institutions the control and auditability they require.

posts.text: Incredible to see this growth!

quotedTweet.text:
We built a $150M ARR business twice.

The first time took 8 years. The second took 2.5.

Today, Podium crossed $150M in AI annual recurring revenue.

Three years ago, we already had a great software business. Well over $100M in revenue, tens of thousands of customers, and a product we'd spent nearly a decade building.

And we decided to start over.

The business was performing well. But we believed AI was going to fundamentally change the software industry and make much of traditional software obsolete.

As a founder, you pour your life into what you're building. An insane amount of time, sacrifice, and effort. The hard part is not getting too attached to it.

When we started building our first AI agents, we had to confront the possibility that much of what we'd built might not be that valuable in the future. That's a tough pill to swallow.

But we also realized those same 10 years had put us in a unique position to take advantage of what AI could do for our customers.

Instead of protecting what we'd spent a decade building, we decided to bet the future of the company on AI employees that actually do the work for our customers.

We massively underestimated what we'd signed up for.

We ended up building entirely new operating systems for the industries we serve, from the AI agents all the way down to the systems of record. Now customers run their entire businesses on Podium.

Reinventing our product wasn't even the hardest part. We had to reinvent how the entire company operated.

When you've been running a company for over a decade, the operational inertia is incredibly powerful. We had to rethink how we build products, how we sell, how we serve customers, and how we run the business.

We effectively started a second startup inside an already successful company. And we're still at the very beginning.

Today, we have 20,000 AI agents working for our customers. They've helped generate more than $13 billion in revenue for those businesses. And we're barely scratching the surface of what AI will be able to do for them.

And we've done all of this while becoming profitable and generating free cash flow. We're building Podium to be around for decades.

Huge credit to our team for having the guts to make this bet and the ability to actually pull it off. We still have a long way to go and tons of problems to solve, but it's so damn fun to be winning when the opportunity ahead is this big.

In the age of AI, you can either disrupt your own company or wait for somebody else to do it.

I'd rather do it ourselves.
quotedTweet.translationZh:
我们两次打造出年经常性收入达1.5亿美元的业务。

第一次用了8年，第二次用了2年半。

今天，Podium 的 AI 业务年经常性收入突破了1.5亿美元。

三年前，我们就已经拥有一家出色的软件公司：收入远超1亿美元，客户数以万计，产品也已打磨了近十年。

但我们决定重新开始。

当时业务发展得很好。但我们相信，AI 将从根本上改变软件行业，让许多传统软件过时。

作为创始人，你会把人生倾注在自己打造的事业中，投入大量时间、牺牲和心血。难的是不对它过于依恋。

开始开发第一批 AI 智能体时，我们不得不面对一种可能：过去打造的许多东西，未来或许不再那么有价值。这很难接受。

但我们也意识到，正是这十年的积累，让我们具备了独特优势，能够利用 AI 为客户创造价值。

我们决定不再守着十年来打造的成果，而是把公司的未来押在能真正替客户干活的 AI 员工身上。

我们严重低估了这件事的难度。

最终，我们为所服务的行业构建了全新的运营系统，从 AI 智能体一直延伸到底层的核心业务记录系统。如今，客户的全部业务都在 Podium 上运行。

重塑产品甚至还不是最难的。我们还得重塑整家公司的运作方式。

一家公司经营十多年后，运营惯性会变得极其强大。我们必须重新思考如何开发产品、如何销售、如何服务客户，以及如何经营公司。

实际上，我们在一家已经成功的公司内部，进行了第二次创业。而我们仍处于起步阶段。

如今，我们有20,000个 AI 智能体为客户工作，已帮助这些企业创造超过130亿美元的收入。而对于 AI 未来能为他们做的事，我们才刚刚触及皮毛。

在做到这一切的同时，我们还实现了盈利，并产生了自由现金流。我们要让 Podium 成为一家长久经营数十年的公司。

这一切都要归功于我们的团队：既有勇气押上这一注，也有能力真正做到。前路还很长，要解决的问题也很多，但眼前的机会如此巨大，能不断取得胜利，真是太痛快了。

在 AI 时代，你要么主动颠覆自己的公司，要么等着别人来颠覆。

我更愿意由我们自己动手。

While I was writing this, my AI assistant got cut off by a bio safety filter. It was summarizing my own team's notes on the model we released today 😅

Frontier labs are moving fast into biology but the scientists and clinicians who'd get the most out of these models are unfortunately the ones running into walls like this one (and every day).

So we partnered with TIGEM (Telethon Institute of Genetics and Medicine), Naple "Federico II" University and Zhongguancun Academy to train Carbon-X.

Carbon-X is an open 14B model that reads raw DNA and talks about it in plain English. On our DNA benchmarks it scores 67%, vs 61% for Claude Opus 5.5 and 50% for Gemini 4 Argon, and its within a point of GPT-6.1 Sol at about 1000x lower cost.

We kept human and animal viruses out of the training data. The weights are open and the model runs on hardware accessible to academia (a laptop).

One example from the blog: give frontier models an 8kb stretch of the NF1 gene with a mutation at a splice site. Most of them call it benign, refuse, or run out of tokens. Carbon-X says pathogenic, because the mutation breaks the splice site.

This century, biology may be where AI matters most. We want to get there with the safety work done in the open and every lab in the world able to build on it. Go try it, and tell us what you find.

OCRia-1 is really, really good at parsing complex tables: nested headers, merged cells, irregular grids, scanned tables, and more. It is also fantastic at parsing complex unlabeled charts (line, bar, pie, technical diagrams), and preserving complex formatting. Most real-world enterprise documents contain at least one of the these, whether it’s a big tax withholding table or a public economic report.

It is a 4B model and outperforms all other models within a similar parameter class: LightOnOCR-3, Chandra-OCR 2, Mistral OCR 4.1, and more. It is also extremely fast.

All credit goes to our research team, who spent countless hours on curating a diverse dataset, tuning our training pipeline, and squeezing every last drop out of model optimization so that it can process billions of pages at scale. 

OCRia-1 as a base is powering all of our modes within LlamaParse (cost-effective, agentic, agentic plus), so you can access its capabilities today! 

If you’re processing millions/billions of documents at scale, we’re offering enterprises that book a demo up to $3k in credits for a guided evaluation.**

reviewedPosts.author: Xudong07452910
reviewedPosts.text:
一个错误如果被 Agent 总结成 Skill，下一次它可能会更自信地再犯一遍。

《More Memory, Worse Agents》研究的就是这种 Error Reproduction。

很多 Agent Memory 会把过去轨迹总结成规则和经验，再用于后续任务。问题在于，一旦总结本身出了偏差，错误也会跟着长期保存，并继续影响之后的决策。

作者因此提出 Anti-Persistence：

真实轨迹和结果可以长期保存，但抽象出来的规则和策略只在当前任务临时生成，用完就丢。下一次再根据新的上下文重新总结。

实验覆盖 ALFWorld、WebShop 和 ScienceWorld。Anti-Persistence 在 9 个模型×任务组合里拿到 7 个最好结果，平均成功率 59.9%，同时 LLM 调用成本最低。

长期保存，并不天然等于长期学习。我的判断是：该长期存的是事实（轨迹和结果），而不是结论（规则和策略）。结论随时可以重新算，存错了却很难发现。

做 Agent Memory 或 Skill 自进化的可以先收藏。我会先检查自己的 Memory 里存的是原始轨迹还是总结出的规则；如果是规则，至少给每条记上来源轨迹，出错时能追回去。

如果某类错误在接入 Memory 之后反而更频繁了，先怀疑的就该是那几条总结出来的规则。

reviewedPosts.text:
评测分数涨了，Agent 实际却没变好。做 Eval 最怕的就是这种「假进步」，而且它往往不是 Prompt 的问题，是 Eval 本身的问题。

Anthropic 这篇工程博客讲的就是怎么避免它，还把整套流程做成了 Claude Code 的两个命令。

① /claude-api build-eval

自动构建评估集，优先从真实任务和失败案例中选题，还会检查评分器是否稳定。同一份输出判两次，如果结果不一致，就得先检查 Eval。

② /claude-api hillclimb

让 Claude 自动改进 Prompt、Skill 或 Harness，每轮提出一项修改，再用训练集和留出测试集验证。

如果训练集分数涨了，测试集却没提升，就撤回修改，避免 Agent 只记住几个失败案例。

而且当连续优化没有效果时，它还会反过来检查 Eval 本身有没有问题，比如题目含糊、评分规则写错。

实际案例中，他们在 44 个客服工单上做优化，最终把单次成本降到了约 1/5，留出集准确率从 78.6% 提升到 90.5%。不过样本量不大，还不能直接推广。

我觉得最值得抄的是两步：评分器判两次看是否一致，以及优化卡住时让 Agent 反过来质疑 Eval。评分器自己都不稳，后面分数的涨跌就没有意义。

但有一点要注意：每轮都用测试集决定是否保留修改，测试集其实也在参与调参。如果用它跑自动 hillclimb，我会额外留一份完全没碰过的数据，在那份数据上不涨，就说明是在给测试集调参，该回滚。

做 Agent Eval、或者正在手动调 Prompt 和 Skill 的，建议先收藏。

reviewedPosts.author: Xudong07452910
reviewedPosts.text:
Agent Harness 也开始学「面向对象编程」了。

Google Cloud AI Research 和 UIUC 这篇 OO-Harness，把 Harness 组织成一棵可以持续进化的类继承树。

不同任务需要的执行策略并不一样。与其不断修改一套全局 Harness，OO-Harness 会先从执行轨迹里找到相似的失败模式，再为这类任务生成一个专门的子类。

公共能力从父类继承，特殊需求只改对应方法。

到了新任务，Router 会先观察基础 Harness 的执行轨迹，再决定继续用 Base，还是切到某个专用 Harness。

这个设计还有一个挺实用的好处：

遇到完全陌生的 OOD 任务时，Router 可以直接退回原始 Base，避免之前学到的「优化」反过来拖累新任务。

实验覆盖 AutomationBench、Workspace-Bench 和 Toolathlon-GYM，OO-Harness 三项都拿到最佳结果。

其中 AutomationBench 从 61.62 提升到 77.41；消融里，真正使用继承结构也比扁平复制 Harness 高近 5 个百分点。

这样的话，Harness 开始有了「分支」和「继承」。

以后面对越来越复杂的任务，Agent 可能不会再共用一套万能工作流。

它的运行系统会像软件架构一样，逐渐长出不同分支，再根据任务选择最合适的一条。

📎 arxiv: https://t.co/aWESW1MpQc

reviewedPosts.text:
花 50 美元编造 5 万条统计数据，最后竟然混进了学术论文和银行研报。

Peec AI 一位研究员几个月前做了个有意思的实验。

他用 GPT-4.1 一天生成了 5 万个统计页面，所有数字都是编的，然后发布到一个新网站上。

结果 Google 的搜索曝光很快跌了下去，ChatGPT 却还在持续访问。作者称，最近 30 天就有约 7.2 万次 ChatGPT-User 请求。

为什么会这样？

作者发现，AI 在检索资料时，很喜欢搜索带有年份的具体统计数据。这些页面刚好提供了现成的数字，检索相关性很高，却缺少真实的数据支撑。

更麻烦的是，这些假数据被论文、研报等引用后，可能进一步获得「权威背书」，让后续的 AI 和读者更难发现问题。

感觉这对做 Research Agent 的人很有启发。Agent 虽然能找到来源、附上引用，离真正可靠的研究还有一段距离。

以后做 Eval，恐怕也得仔细查一下引用的数据究竟有没有可靠的原始出处？

推荐 OpenAI 刚公开的 ChatGPT 广告系统的工程架构，没想到背后居然跑着一个专门负责广告投放的 Agent。

传统广告主要靠搜索词判断需求，但 ChatGPT 用户经常聊了好几轮，才逐渐暴露出购买意图。

为此，OpenAI 专门训练了一个 LLM 调度器，让它理解多轮对话，再通过 Tool Call 完成广告检索、筛选、相关性评估和竞价。最终价格仍由独立的拍卖系统决定。

我觉得最漂亮的是它的隔离设计。

广告 Agent 和 ChatGPT 正常回答并行运行。即便广告竞价成功，只要来晚了就直接放弃，绝不拖慢用户的回复。

另外，他们还用更强的模型复盘投放记录，结合用户反馈，持续训练和改进负责执行的模型。

这套系统上线不到 200 天，广告业务的年化收入就达到 10 亿美元。

这样看来，Agent 真正进入生产环境后，除了模型能力，系统边界、失败回退和持续评估可能才是更值得花时间打磨的地方。

reviewedPosts.text:
What I Talk About When I Talk About Control

Making something and having the skill to make it used to feel tightly linked. Now the outcome no longer proves you have the skill. Or does it?

When text-to-video first started working, that’s what it felt like. All you had to do was type in a short text description, press a button, and voila. It was magic or cheating, depending on how you looked at it. The fact that it worked at all was a breakthrough, but it also didn’t look like the person making the thing had done very much. We’d created something like auto mode for generative video, and “auto” isn’t a word we associate with craft. Yes, prompting is a skill, but being a better “describer” of the thing you want to make isn’t something we’ve historically been satisfied with as skill, unless your craft itself was flowery prose.

As the models get more capable, the makers want more degrees of freedom to try things. New places to make choices become new places to exercise judgment, and enough judgment creates the possibility of craft. Creators start developing intuitions about the models, just like people have developed intuitions about cameras, editing software, or any other medium.

New capabilities show up before we can understand them. So we build whatever interface we can manage to. Minimum viable control and minimum interfaces to get started. That becomes the first auto mode for that new tool. Then people use it, push it against its limits, and give us pretty loud hints at what they want to be able to do next. It takes time to figure out which new primitives are powerful, and where users want more control.

People want more control. And they want more degrees of freedom. I believe that part of what makes models more controllable is that they become personal. AI is fundamentally a general purpose technology that can be shaped in any unique way you want. Models are generalization machines that can adapt to what you need. Everyone has a different way of using models. Different ways of finding them useful and productive.

I strongly believe that most of the interfaces we use to control models will be individual-specific instead of general. Not many to one, but one to one. Any form of control you can imagine. Any version of Runway you want. Soon.

reviewedPosts.text:
This is exactly why banks need to work with @PaymanAI

Instead of third-party agents scraping logins, @PaymanAI deploys AI agents inside the bank, on the institution’s existing systems.

The agent only acts when an authenticated customer asks. An immutable policy engine (deliberately not an LLM) checks every proposed action against the bank’s rules before anything touches the core. Every step is logged in a complete audit trail - the customer’s exact words, how the AI interpreted them, which policies applied, and what executed.

The bank holds the kill switch. Payman is SOC 2 Type II and integrates with cores like FIS, Fiserv, and Jack Henry without replacing them.

In practice, that means a customer can say “Pay my ConEd bill” or “Move $1,850 to cover rent” and get it done in seconds, with confirmation - under the bank’s brand, policies, and oversight. Community banks are already partnering with them (Middlesex Federal, Citizens State Bank in Colorado). It’s backed by Visa, Coinbase Ventures, and Circle, and it recently won the ICBA ThinkTECH Banker’s Choice Award.

This story shows what happens when AI meets banking without a trust layer: chaos, blocks, and lost convenience. Payman is the missing piece, the orchestration layer that lets people get the helpful AI banking experience they want, while giving institutions the control and auditability they require.
